Masked Butcher: Turning the Entire Serpentspine into a Blood-Moon Altar

Region (English scoring-table grouping): Serpentspine.

Flag

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 94/100 | Autocracy 95/100 | Magic–Artifice 95/100 (100 = Magic, 0 = Artifice; thematic intensity 95/100) | Pluralism 5/100. The v2.1 value is Evil (0/100), with a Stable trajectory. Massacres, making masks from flayed skin, blood sacrifice, and confining multiple sapient peoples as an ongoing blood supply are embedded in the state system, making this an extreme case of reducing people to resources and denying their personhood.

You are not building an orcish state to be understood; you are running a theocratic war machine powered by plunder, sacrifice, masks, and the Blood Moon.

Narrative: High | Mission-tree length: Long (36 direct missions) | Mission-tree update: current local files updated through 2026-09-07 | Distinctiveness: Very high | Tedium: Medium-high | Early pressure: High | Expansion capacity: High

Identity and History

The Masked Butcher (H81) is a Black Orc warband in the southern Serpentspine in 1444, with its capital at Bloodied Altar, following Old Dookan, and using the Dwarovar Warband government. It is ruled by Vrirrig Beardbutcher. [Local history script] The current offline Wiki adds only three points: they are a native Black Orc group of the Serpentspine, based in the Serpentreach, and the clan already existed during the Greentide. The page itself is a short stub and cannot support a fuller clan history. [Wiki] [Unverified]

Black Orc history reaches far earlier than the Greentide wars in the Serpentspine. A prior research note attributes to the offline Wiki the claim that Black Orcs entered the southern Serpentspine from the Agroloth Confluence around 5400 BA, but that passage does not appear in the Wiki chunks actually retrieved for this entry; treat the date and route as unverified pending a pinpointed source. Even if accurate, it concerns Black Orc migration as a whole; it would not establish that the Masked Butcher clan already existed, took part in that incursion, or had a traceable succession of leaders. The clan's own founder and migration date remain unsupported by reliable records; its substantial national story begins in mission narratives after 1444. [Prior Wiki attribution; not confirmed in retrieved chunks] [Unverified]

National Story and Campaign Arc

The Masked Butcher's opening is a typical Serpentspine Black Orc start: colonize the caverns, complete expeditions, capture holds, and turn the stockpiles of spoils around Bloodied Altar into the center of the state. [Local scripts] But expansion is not an end in itself. Every war seeks blood for the altar, victims for the mask-carvers, and the conditions needed to awaken a power sleeping underground.

As the warband pushes deeper into the mountains, the worship of Old Dookan is reshaped into a cult centered on blood, moonlight, and masks. The state moves from a tribal warband toward a theocracy, with the mage estate managing the power of the masks; after vampires intervene in succession and ritual, rule increasingly depends on bloodlines, sacrifice, and control of the altar. [Local flavour text] Missions also tell the story of adventurers trying to end the disaster, making the campaign more than an “evil conquest checklist”: it is a horror story in which the player inhabits the monster and then sees its victims resist.

In the later stages, the campaign leaves the Serpentspine and advances into Deepwoods, Ourdia, Bahar, and Bulwar. The endgame calls for bringing large regions under one faith and strengthening Blood Rage and the “True Night”; this is no redemption route, but an escalation from a local cult to a cross-regional order of night. [Local scripts]

Core Mechanics

  1. Spoils Pile and altar moonlight: You choose and expand a spoils pile near the altar, increasing its strength. Strength affects the mage estate, missionary capacity, mask capacity, and later rituals; taking land is not enough—you must keep channeling the gains from plunder back to the heartland.
  2. Trading blood for religious power: Plunder, war, and sacrifice provide religious power for Blood Rage, summoning the Blood Moon, and carving masks. The Blood Moon changes stability and rebellion conditions at home and in neighboring countries, tying religious actions to the pace of war.
  3. Racial masks and the mage estate: Victims from different races unlock different masks. Masks can be upgraded, while the number of powerful versions that can be equipped at once is limited. Expanding mage privileges and altar strength creates room to stack more effects. This is a build system that changes with the targets of conquest, not an ordinary permanent modifier.
  4. “Reserves” and ongoing sacrifice: Missions and decisions turn populations such as goblins, dwarves, halflings, trolls, ogres, kobolds, centaurs, and others into controlled sources of reserves. This meets the cult's long-term demand for blood and mask materials, and is the institutional core of this route's darkest practices. [Local scripts]

Play by Phase

At the start, survive and open the colonization route. You need to acquire institutions, complete underground expeditions, and establish a secure hinterland around Bloodied Altar. Early military strength is useful, but migration, colonization, and waiting for events can slow the pace. In the middle game, connect the spoils pile, theocratic reforms, vampire succession, mage privileges, and the first high-tier masks, while continually seeking new races as sources for masks and reserves.

Beyond the mountains, the loop becomes conquer a new region → establish reserves → plunder and sacrifice → strengthen the altar and masks → use the new abilities to launch the next conquest. The mission scope eventually spans the Serpentspine, Deepwoods, and Bulwar. Warfare is extensive and diplomacy has little value. The real bottleneck is not a lack of casus belli, but whether colonization time, mask events, religious power, and mission gates can advance in step.

Formables and Endgame

The Masked Butcher has no dedicated successor Tag. Any eligible Serpentspine Orc can form the Black Sun (Karashar, Z57) through a generic decision, and H81 could in principle take that route; however, the decision changes the Tag, culture, and religion and replaces the mission tree, while the H81 mission group explicitly excludes Z57. [Local scripts] Karashar is therefore an optional detour that leaves the Masked Butcher-specific campaign, not the endpoint of this continuous campaign chain, and it is not counted as completed alongside this entry.

The H81 route's own endgame instead expands the altar system, suppresses adventurer resistance, spreads the Blood Moon cult across Bulwari regions, and makes the night and Blood Rage permanent national powers.

Personality and Recommendation

EOIV: It is extremely expansionist, concentrating order through theocracy, mages, and the altar; its mask builds, vampire institutions, and assembly of cross-racial abilities are strongly innovative; and its ultimate goal is to turn a local cult into a worldwide Blood Moon vision. Its moral orientation is Evil (0/100, high confidence): institutionalized sacrifice, treating peoples as a renewable blood supply, taking victims' skin to make masks, and spreading a terrifying order through large-scale conquest are not offset by any protective aims.

Recommended for players who enjoy a monster's point of view, dark narratives, relentless conquest, build-oriented national mechanics, and text-heavy campaigns. Avoid it if you dislike waiting for colonization and events, managing several layers of resources, or playing a route whose state institutions explicitly revolve around slaughter and sacrifice.

Community Experience and Evidentiary Limits

[Official dev diaries] The 2024-11 dev diary previewed this country through adventurers investigating the blood altar and Blood Moon; the month-12 Fires of Conviction release announcement confirmed that the mission tree shipped with that version. The current implementation should still be checked against local scripts.

[Community accounts] A guide for a pre-release test branch recommends acquiring institutions early, moving to Arg-Ordstun, and planning the capital around the altar. A post-release play report describes long waits for early colonization and the halfling-mask event, but its comments do not agree on whether these are mechanics, old-version issues, or Mod conflicts. These accounts show differences in player experience; they do not prove a fixed defect in the current version.

The local offline Wiki status is ok, but the country page is a stub; pre-1444 history remains the main evidence gap. The figure 36 is the direct-mission count in the current structured index, not a claim that every mission will necessarily be visible or completed in a single campaign.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the idea set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested in the group, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only the national ideas themselves are listed; racial, government, or mission rewards are not mixed into these values. Idea sets shown as alternatives or with separate conditions are not assumed to stack; whether a new set is accepted on formation depends on the actual event or decision and the player's choice. Idea text may recount history or describe a future ideal; it does not automatically mean the events have already occurred by 1444.

Masked Butcher (H81) — Masked Butcher Ideas

Traditions: Masked Butcher Traditions

Effects: Infantry combat ability: +10%; Land attrition: -15%.

Idea 1: Bogeyman of the Serpentreach

A monster is said to haunt the dark caverns and crumbling halls of the Serpentreach: the Masked Butcher. It has been described as an orc who wears a mask made from the flesh of his victims and paints its skin with their blood. To some, it is but a myth that personifies the horrors of the Dwarovar, but it is all too real to us...

Because we are the Masked Butcher. It is not one beast that hunts these halls but our entire people. There is no limit to what counts as our prey, and in times of war, these eerie tales and our clan's hunting tradition translate well into guerrilla tactics and strike fear into any armies that dare enter our land.

Effect: Hostile attrition: +100%.

Idea 2: Trophy Hunts

When a young orc of the clan reaches maturity, they must face a rite of passage: they are sent off on a hunt, only returning when they have proven themselves. A young orc may go weeks before returning home, returning loaded down with slaughtered prey.

The kills will be stripped of loot and body parts to act as trophies but the greatest of the kills will have its flesh removed and turned into a mask for the newly matured orc. This mask signifies the beginning of an orc's life as a hunter and is worn as a mark of prestige and rank in the clan's hierarchy.

Effects: Prestige from land battles: +0.5; Legitimacy: +0.5; Devotion: +0.5; Republican tradition: +0.15; Horde unity: +0.5.

Idea 3: Empty Halls, Empty Throne

For ages, our clan was small and our deeds were merely chalked up as a monster in myth. That was until most orcs began leaving the Serpentreach in droves for the Western Dwarovar. One of our most powerful neighbors left behind its throne and a magnificent altar lit up by natural light from above.

No sign could be clearer that we, the orcs who stayed behind, were destined to rule the Serpentreach. Now, many years have passed since we claimed this throne and we have grown far beyond the small clan we once were. Our population continues to boom and with all the open space and little to no competition, our expansion outward sees no end in sight.

Effect: Global colonial growth: +2000%.

Idea 4: Yash-Vultog

A term that roughly translates to "The Count", our clan values what you have killed and the quality of that kill as that is what truly shows strength. On the battlefield, our orcs are savage as all seek to raise their rank in the clan by killing more and slaying the greatest foe. Even better if an orc can take them alive, as a sacrifice in front of all to see makes it undisputed that you killed them.

In every battle, the best rises above the rest. In every battle, the rest try to rise above the best. This way of life makes it to where our troops are always inspired to improve and learn from every fight to do better in the next while our generals are always made up of the greatest among them.

Effect: Army tradition from battles: +1.

Idea 5: Where The Blood Moon Shines

All could see me standing in the dim light with my hand placed over the chest of my captive who lay flat on the altar, and yet I couldn’t see anything beyond but the surrounding pitch black and a few stars just barely peeking through from above. Silence, even from those who wished not to be, filled this cavern to the brim. Nothing had ever tested my patience before more than this uneasy excitement for a passing light to say go. The skylight began to shift to a deep red and the moment the Moon slightly emerged I struck with unparalleled strength and tore out the heart of my captive and held it up high towards the light. Two types of screams followed: cheers and cries. As the red moonlight began to pour into the cavern banishing that pitch black darkness, I finally could see the hundreds of orcs in wait rushing forward dragging their captives with them toward the altar. It only lasted about an hour but more blood was spilt in that time than any night before it. Throughout the celebration, I could only think about the nights that have yet to come.

-Chieftain Vrirrig Beardbutcher's account of the first accurately predicted blood moon.

Effect: Prestige: +1.

Idea 6: Temple of Crimson

The throne and altar are the center of our clan. Thousands live nearby while thousands more flock in to make sacrifices there. Unfortunately, the cave the throne and altar lie in was never meant to support such a vast population and influx of travelers.

To amend this overcrowding, we will undertake a massive excavation and redesign of this cavern. We shall build a central structure that reaches up higher towards the light, with the altar at the very top alongside the Chief's expanded throne room. Around this structure, we shall carve roads and lesser dwellings, to smooth travel and create efficient residences. What started as no more than a bloodied altar will become the beating heart of these mountains.

Effect: Development cost: -10%.

Idea 7: Bala-karvash

We are Bala-karvash, "Apex Predators". We are hunters in search of the deadliest game. The very top of the food chain. The bravest warriors quickly learn that bravado will not save them from our diligence. The toughest soldiers quickly learn that strength will not save them from our physical superiority. The mightiest beasts quickly learn that instinct will not save them from our tactics.

All quickly learn that they are the ones being hunted. Whether in the bushes or out on the open battlefield, we hold out and wait for the perfect opportunity then pounce when the moment is right.

Effect: morale_damage_received: -10%.

Ambition: Masked Butcher Ambition

Effect: Years of separatism: -5.
